thread: FOI/EIR 00211484 — commemorative tree, Church View Close / Great House Farm
subject: 00211484 — narrowed request — commemorative tree, Church View Close / Great House Farm
body:
Information Governance Team,
Vale of Glamorgan Council
FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

Case 00211484. This narrows the request. It does not reopen 00210772. Please keep them separate.

I hold dated photographs of the works. Please disclose:

1. The instruction, works order or contractor record for removal of the commemorative tree on or adjoining the former Great House Farm / Church View Close land.
2. The date of the works and who authorised them.
3. Any note linking the tree to the Williams / Buckler family, to Mary Williams, or to the 1988 demolition.

If nothing is held, say what was searched.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . This request is about one tree and one works record. It is not a request that you decide title.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
[redacted]

thread: FOI/EIR 00211557 — s.52/land charges, planning register, condition 16–18 chain, 92/00671/RES; missing appendices C, D and E
subject: FOI/EIR — Great House Farm / Church View Close — s.52/land charges, planning register, EA screening, condition 16–18 chain, 92/00671/RES — new request, not 00210772
body:
Information Governance Team
Vale of Glamorgan Council
FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk
cc: planning@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

New request under FOIA 2000 and/or EIR 2004. Do not treat this as a reopening or expansion of 00210772, 00211463 or 00211484. Those cases stay as they are.

Land: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Leckwith Road, Llandough, later Church View Close.
Applications: 89/01396/OUT (outline granted 13 March 1990) and 92/00671/RES.

I already have, or have already asked for, the officer's report, Policy H.2 text, Appendices C–E, the decision notices, and the general archaeological-condition papers. This request is confined to classes that those earlier requests did not name.

Please disclose recorded information held, or confirm item by item if not held:

1. Section 52 / later section 106 / land charges
Any agreement under section 52 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1971, any later section 106 instrument, any deed, undertaking or other agreement regulating the development or use of this land, and any corresponding entry on the local land charges register. Search legal, planning and land-charges holdings, not only the 2026 planning-file scan. If none is held, say so expressly. That is an open records question, not a conclusion that none existed.

2. Historic planning register
The planning-register entries that the Town and Country Planning General Development Order 1988 required the authority to keep for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES: the applications, reserved-matters applications, plans and drawings, and relevant decision information. If the 2026 file disclosure is incomplete against that register, say what the register still lists and what is missing from the file.

3. Appendix B
Appendix B to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT: the further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust. Case 00211463 asked for C, D and E and for a list of annexes. It did not ask for B by that description. If B is not held, say when it left the file, under what retention rule, and whether any copy survives elsewhere.

4. Condition 16–18 chain
Named papers, not a general search:
(a) conditions 16, 17 and 18 as issued on the 13 March 1990 permission;
(b) the Council's October 1990 confirmation of condition 17;
(c) GGAT's archaeological warning of July 1992;
(d) the September 1992 reserved-matters approval, and whether any further archaeological condition was attached;
(e) the 1993–94 papers on whether condition 18 had been discharged, including GGAT's December 1993 letters recommending a breach-of-condition notice.

5. Environmental assessment / screening
Any preliminary environmental-assessment determination, screening opinion, or recorded decision that an environmental statement was or was not required for 89/01396/OUT. The application site is described as about 3.4 acres / 1.38 hectares. I am not asserting that an environmental statement was required. I am asking whether the Council made and recorded the determination at all.

6. Archaeological-interest consultation route
Any record of the statutory consultation route actually used because the land was recorded in the county Sites and Monuments Record, or was treated as a "site of archaeological interest" under the 1988 Order. I am not asking you to treat SMR status as automatic proof of a particular duty. I am asking what route was used.

7. Application receipt date
The Council's receipt record for 89/01396/OUT. The application form is dated October 1989. The reconstructed planning record gives 8 November 1989 as receipt of the application and plans. Please supply the date-stamped receipt, validation or register entry.

8. 92/00671/RES completeness and applicant standing
(a) A file list or register for 92/00671/RES showing what the reserved-matters file originally contained.
(b) Any sale, option, conditional-contract or authority-to-apply paper on the planning files covering the change from BP Properties (1989 outline applicant) to Ideal Homes Wales (appearing on the 1992 reserved-matters trail), including the recorded BP-to-Ideal Homes transfer of 3 December 1993.
This is a documentary interest/authority question. It is not an allegation that the 1992 application was invalid.

If a record is not held, say so for that item. If it was destroyed, transferred or archived, give the date, the schedule, and any surviving catalogue. Search planning, legal, land charges and archived/scanned holdings.

Please give a new reference and the 20 working-day date. Preserve anything in scope.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . I am not asking the Council to decide title.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals
[redacted]

thread: Formal concern, preservation and subject access (Monitoring Officer / DPO / Complaints)
subject: Formal concern, preservation and subject access — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — remedy before escalation
body:
Victoria Davidson
Monitoring Officer and Head of Legal and Democratic Services
Vale of Glamorgan Council
vdavidson@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk
Also: DPO@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk; complaints@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

This is a formal concern, a preservation notice, and a subject access request. It is the opportunity to remedy before the Information Commissioner and, if the internal processes end without remedy, the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales.

I am not asking the Council to decide title. I am asking it to deal with its own records and its own delay.

1. Complete the internal review of FOI/EIR 00210772, requested 7 July 2026, acknowledged 10 July 2026, further apology 11 September 2026, chased 5 August, 1 September and 22 September 2026. There is still no outcome. That is past a reasonable period. An ICO complaint confined to that delay is drafted. A completed review would deal with the point.

2. Preserve planning, building-control, housing, legal, local-land-charge and land records for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, titles WA231076 and WA240304, Church View Close, and the 1988 demolition (possession 29 November 1988; demolition begun 6 December 1988). Stop routine destruction of those files. That hold includes, if held:
- any section 52 TCPA 1971 / later section 106 / deed / undertaking and the matching land-charge entry;
- the 1988 GDO planning-register entries for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES;
- officer-report Appendices B–E (B = further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust);
- conditions 16–18 and the 1990–94 discharge papers, including the October 1990 confirmation of condition 17 and the 1993–94 dispute over condition 18;
- any environmental-assessment / screening determination for the outline application;
- the complete 92/00671/RES file and any BP–Ideal Homes sale, option or conditional-contract paper on the planning files, including the recorded transfer of 3 December 1993.
A separate FOI/EIR for those classes will follow and must not be folded into 00210772, 00211463 or 00211484.

3. Subject access under UK GDPR Article 15: personal data you hold about me, Sion Buckler, in those files, and about Mary Doreen Williams (died 26 March 1983) and William Buckler so far as the law allows a relative to see it. Say what identification you need before the month starts.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . The investigation distinguishes Parcel A (farmhouse, garden, buildings and yard — the family's maintained freehold) from Parcel B (eastern fields — not presently disputed). The 1987 Court of Appeal decided possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the documentary root of Parcel A. Council papers on planning and demolition go to that question. They are not a finding against any officer.

Nothing in this letter abandons any claim concerning title, registration, concealment, limitation, reopening or reparations. This is not a claim form.

Please acknowledge, name the officer for the hold, and give a date for the 00210772 outcome.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals
[redacted]

subject: Preservation notice — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — do not destroy, transfer or dispose
note: Sent jointly to fourteen record holders, including the Council's FOI Unit and DPO. No reply from the Council appears in this thread; replies from other bodies are catalogued on their own pages.
body:
To each recipient, in your own capacity as holder or likely holder of records. Please do not treat this as a joint reply. Answer only for your own holdings.

Sirs/Madam,

This is a preservation notice. It is not a claim form and not service of proceedings. It does not replace any FOI, review or subject access request already with you.

Land: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's. Titles WA231076, WA240304 (closed), WA513690, WA735527, and any related title. Planning refs 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES.

Please preserve, and do not destroy, transfer out of your custody without a written receipt, or dispose of, any file, plan, photograph, tape or electronic record in your possession, custody or control relating to:

1. The 1877 split, the 1916 and 1939 tenancies, and the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance.
2. The 1955 and 1962 possession orders, the 1974 proceedings, and BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2.
3. First registration: WA231076 application 30 November 1982; WA240304 application 23 February 1983; later amalgamation.
4. The 1988 possession (29 November) and demolition (begun 6 December), including listing, planning, police and any liaison papers.
5. Mary Doreen Williams (died 26 March 1983) and William Buckler, so far as your file concerns this land.

Also preserve, if you hold them, the following planning and land-charge classes. Absence from a 2026 file disclosure is not proof they never existed:

6. Any section 52 Town and Country Planning Act 1971 agreement, later section 106 instrument, deed, undertaking or other agreement regulating the development or use of this land, and any corresponding local-land-charge entry.
7. The historic planning-register entries required by the Town and Country Planning General Development Order 1988 for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES (applications, reserved matters, plans and drawings, and decision information).
8. The officer's report annexes to 89/01396/OUT, including Appendix B (further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust), and Appendices C–E.
9. The condition chain on 89/01396/OUT: conditions 16–18; the Council's October 1990 confirmation of condition 17; GGAT's July 1992 archaeological warning; the September 1992 reserved-matters approval; and the 1993–94 papers on whether condition 18 had been discharged.
10. Any preliminary environmental-assessment / screening determination for the outline application (site described as about 3.4 acres / 1.38 ha).
11. Any record of the statutory consultation route used because the land was, or was treated as, a site of archaeological interest / SMR entry under the 1988 Order.
12. The complete 92/00671/RES file, and any sale, option, conditional-contract or transfer paper on the planning files covering BP Properties to Ideal Homes Wales, including the recorded transfer of 3 December 1993.
13. The application-receipt record for 89/01396/OUT (form dated October 1989; reconstructed Council receipt 8 November 1989).

Please stop routine deletion, including archived mailboxes, for anything in that scope.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . The investigation distinguishes the farmhouse parcel from the eastern fields. The 1987 Court of Appeal decided possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the documentary root of the farmhouse parcel. These records go to that question. This notice is not a finding against any of you.

Please acknowledge, name the officer responsible for the hold, and say what you hold in scope. If you hold nothing, say what you searched.

Nothing in this letter abandons any claim concerning title, registration, concealment, limitation, reopening or alteration of the register.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals
[redacted]

thread: Cllr Christopher Franks — Great House Farm, Llandough
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough
body:
Chris,

I flew back, I'm even at Mamgus old house in Dinas from time to time.

Here's a website AI generated and maintains which articulates my grievance.
https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

I shared with the charity who own the woodland. They're immidiate response
was to do what everyone has always done to us and ignore our ownership
claim and assertion and acknowledge someone else as the owner.

Many and myself are still investigating. But in a nutshell a synthetic
parcel appears to have been created, based on enough years of attempts to
make our occupancy appear permissive, so that the land registry can accept
the story. So 1974 licence letters was also a failed attempt and premis my
family rejected, in a long line of failed attempts spanning back to at
least 1949.

The registration then made the 1987 ruling possible. And that ruling is
what the land registry depend on to justify its decision to allow BP to
register a synthetic mimic of our parcel in their names, without notifying
us until long after the appeal of that registration had ended. In which my
nan conveniently died. Equally that 1987 ruling depends on the 1983
registration of our land parcel (or mimic synthetic version of it, built
from a falsehood of a chain that didn't have root title and was not and
never was successful attempts to make our occupancy permissive.

Furthermore the "whole farm" being treated as one parcel, was not merged
back into one parcel (a synthetic version of our parcel too, not ours),
until after the 1986/1987 case.

So my nan Mary Williams didn't get a fair opportunity to reject the licence
letter in 1974 between it being offered and quashing the 1962 possession
order for our land parcel. Which itself was never enforced and arguably not
legally enforceable as it was based on ambuguity from the 1955 order which
made our occupancy of our parcel simply appear permissive with concealment
of the fact my nans resistence was due to her ownership claim. And
concealment of the fact "whole farm" excluded our parcel of land and was
not in the 1939 tenancy agreement. So not conveyed to Western Ground Rents
in 1938.

Further to that my nans ownership claim, even though unable to be proven
due her title being stolen in 1950/52, still means having not paid anyone
for anything on her parcel since 1928 she will have already qualified for
adverse possession by 1940.

We didn't get fair opportunity to appeal the 83 registration either. We
also didn't get opportunity to appeal CADWs decision to not list our county
treasure 800 year old home as a grade II before BP demolished it at 4am the
next day.

Then the council didn't hold them to any account when they returned in 1989
to get planning permission. The council are also under the microscope for
many failures. Failure to issue a demolition block order. Also two annexes
are missing from those planning docs which are local historic societies
testemony to petition demolition citing our old ancestral homes
significants (home since 1667 and my birth home I remind you).

Please just look at the evidence.
https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

My family are living like hostages under terrorists and have done for 38
years. It's not acceptable. This demonic realm and spell has to be fought
off.

Do what you can please. Even if its a small prayer for us. I thank you in
advance.

See attached a few images from my military service. I served this country.
I'm still trying to here. I left my career with full honours. My last
employer in the Vale Council. I hope this betrayal will end. I'm more than
disappointed in local authories here, who don't appear any less hostile to
my family and our interest in our land in Llandough.

I can't play the role of hostage or prisoner of war under this regime. My
family are mostly all women and children, I am not. It's an untenable
situation Chris. The Senedd should have at least done a public enquiry of
this.

Regards,

Sion Hywel Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/ Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: FOI/EIR 00211463 — planning appendices C, D, E and Policy H.2 (89/01396/OUT)
subject: Re: FOI/EIR request - Case Ref/ 00211463 — clarification and refinement of request
body:
Freedom of Information Officer,

Case Ref: 00211463 — request received 17 September 2026

I write to clarify and refine the above request while it remains open,
having now examined the original manuscript of the planning officer's
report rather than a transcription. My earlier request named two
organisations; the document in fact identifies the correspondents
differently, and I ask that the request be read as follows.

The passage relied upon
The planning officer's report on application 89/01396/OUT (residential
development including new access road, land at Great House Farm, Leckwith
Road, Llandough, Penarth; outline permission granted 13 March 1990) states,
at page 2:

"Two letters have been received from the Barry Preservation Society and
Civic Trust and a local County Councillor (who is a member of the Glamorgan
Gwent Archaeological Trust) making representations in respect of this
application and a copy of both these letters are attached to this report as
Appendices 'C' and 'D' respectively."

The following paragraph of the same report states:

"The Applicants' Agents have written in response to the report of the
Glamorgan Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd. on the site and a copy of this
letter is attached to this report as Appendix 'E'."

What I request
Appendix "C" to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT — the letter from the
Barry Preservation Society and Civic Trust.

Appendix "D" — the letter from the local County Councillor referred to,
together with that Councillor's name.

Appendix "E" — the letter from the Applicants' Agents responding to the
report of the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd.

A list of all appendices ("A" to "E" or further) to that officer's report,
so that the complete annex set is identified.

Any register, index, schedule or file list for application 89/01396/OUT
recording the documents originally held on the file.
A further document referred to in the same report

The officer's report also records, of the East Vale Local Plan:

"The greater part of the land is allocated for new residential development
in the East Vale Local Plan (Policy No. H.2.) The information supporting
the policy states that buildings on the site should be retained, however
were unfortunately demolished a little while ago."

I therefore also request:
The text of Policy H.2 of the East Vale Local Plan and the supporting
information to that policy referred to above, in the version current in
1989–1990.

Points on handling
These are documents the Council's own report states were attached to it. If
any of them is not held, I ask the Council to say so expressly, and to
state (a) when it ceased to be held, (b) under what retention schedule or
disposal decision, and (c) whether any record of that disposal exists. A
response that "no additional information has been identified" would not
address a request for annexes that the Council's own report records as
attached.

I note the Council's letter of 11 September 2026 in a related matter, which
stated that "further historical documentation has been found... not
necessarily Council documentation but is nonetheless in the Council's
possession". I ask that this material be searched in responding to the
present request.

I intend this as a clarification and refinement of case 00211463 under the
Council's duty to advise and assist (s.16 FOIA 2000 / reg. 9 EIR 2004), and
not as a new request. If the Council takes the view that any part of it
must be treated as a fresh request, please confirm that in writing,
identify which parts, and give the revised due date, so that I am not left
uncertain which deadline applies to which element.
I should be grateful for confirmation of receipt.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
